hints: A brute force of checking every pair is O(n²). Can you do it in one pass?
For each number x, the partner you need is target - x. How can you check quickly whether you've already seen it?
A hash map from value → index answers that lookup in O(1).
edgeCases: Duplicate values that form the answer, e.g. [3,3] with target 6
two-sum.explanation: You must return positions (indices), not the numbers themselves. Since exactly one answer exists you can stop at the first pair found. n up to 10^4 means O(n²) passes but O(n) is the expected interview answer.

hints: The most recent unmatched opening bracket must be closed first — which data structure gives you 'most recent'?
Push openers; on a closer, the top of the stack must be its pair.
edgeCases: Unclosed openers left at the end like "("
Interleaved types like "([)]" which is invalid
valid-parentheses.explanation: Validity means correct type AND correct nesting order. An empty stack at the end means every opener was closed.

hints: Negative numbers can never be palindromes because of the '-' sign.
Try reversing only half of the digits to avoid overflow.
palindrome-number.explanation: A palindrome reads the same both ways. Converting to string is simplest; the follow-up asks you to do it mathematically.

hints: Sorted array + O(log n) requirement = binary search.
When the loop ends without finding target, the left pointer is exactly the insert position.
edgeCases: Target larger than all elements → n
search-insert-position.explanation: You're looking for the first index whose value is ≥ target (the lower bound).

hints: To reach step n you came from step n-1 or n-2.
ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2). Does that look familiar?
edgeCases: n = 45 (largest answer still fits in 32-bit int)
climbing-stairs.explanation: This is the Fibonacci recurrence. Plain recursion is exponential; memoize or iterate.

hints: You must buy before you sell.
Track the minimum price seen so far and the best profit if you sold today.
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.explanation: One transaction only. Answer is max over days of (price - lowest earlier price), never negative.

hints: A set stores unique values.
Alternatively, after sorting, duplicates become neighbours.
contains-duplicate.explanation: Return as soon as any value repeats. Set gives O(n) time, sorting gives O(1) extra space.

hints: Different lengths can never be anagrams.
Count each letter's frequency in s and subtract for t.
edgeCases: Same letters, different counts like "aacc" vs "ccac"
valid-anagram.explanation: Anagrams use exactly the same multiset of characters.

hints: Use a sliding window [start, i] that never contains a repeat.
Remember the last index of each character; when you see a repeat inside the window, jump start past it.
edgeCases: "abba" — the old 'a' is outside the window
longest-substring-without-repeating-char.explanation: Substring means contiguous (unlike subsequence). Each character enters and leaves the window at most once → O(n).

hints: If the running sum becomes negative, it can only hurt future subarrays.
Kadane: cur = max(x, cur + x).
edgeCases: All negative numbers → the largest single element
maximum-subarray.explanation: The subarray must be non-empty, so initialise with the first element, not 0.

hints: answer[i] = product of everything on the left × product of everything on the right.
Compute left products in one pass and right products in a second pass.
edgeCases: Two or more zeros → all zeros
product-of-array-except-self.explanation: Division is not allowed (and fails with zeros). Prefix/suffix products solve it in O(n).

hints: Area = min(height[l], height[r]) × (r - l).
Start with the widest container; moving the taller line can never help, so move the shorter one.
container-with-most-water.explanation: Two pointers turn the O(n²) pair search into O(n).

hints: Track the farthest index you can reach so far.
If the current index is beyond that farthest reach, you are stuck.
edgeCases: Single element → already at the end
Zero at the first position with more elements
jump-game.explanation: Each value is the maximum jump, you may jump less. Greedy reach tracking is O(n).

hints: Water above bar i = min(maxLeft, maxRight) - height[i].
Precompute max-left and max-right arrays, or use two pointers moving from the side with the smaller max.
trapping-rain-water.explanation: Think per column, not per pool. The lower of the two tallest walls on each side decides the water level.

hints: Merging works in O(m+n). For O(log), binary search a partition of the smaller array.
A correct partition has maxLeft1 ≤ minRight2 and maxLeft2 ≤ minRight1.
median-of-two-sorted-arrays.explanation: Median = middle element (odd total) or average of two middle elements (even total). Output is compared to 5 decimals.

hints: Define dp[i][j] = min edits to convert word1[:i] to word2[:j].
If characters match, dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]; otherwise 1 + min(insert, delete, replace).
edgeCases: Either string empty → length of the other
edit-distance.explanation: Classic Levenshtein distance. Base cases: converting to/from an empty string costs its length.

hints: Check 8 directions around the King.
Find the nearest queen in each direction.
